name: pulse
displayName: Pulse (one command that pulls and analyses app monitoring)
description: A single command that pulls crashes, store reviews and ratings, product analytics, revenue and backend health into one dated snapshot, renders a report, and lets the agent narrate it against the previous run. Every source resolves to ok / missing / unavailable, and an unavailable source is never rendered as a zero.

notes: No runtime dependencies and nothing in the app bundle. Node 18+ for global fetch; ES256 JWT is signed with node:crypto and gzip with node:zlib.
CommonJS .js on purpose, never .mjs: a ts-jest/CommonJS suite cannot require an ESM module, so an .mjs source would be untestable. Node runs it directly either way.

Crashlytics has NO public REST read API. The script cannot fetch it; the slash command gathers it through the Firebase MCP server and hands it over as a JSON file. That asymmetry is deliberate and documented rather than hidden behind a wrapper.
Sources are all optional. A missing credential makes one source (or one block of one source) unavailable and never fails the run.

env.why: NEVER the app's .env. In an Expo/EAS app the client .env is uploaded to the build servers so public keys reach the bundle; a server secret there ships to the build infrastructure. The .env.*.local pattern is already ignored by git and .easignore.

placeholders.what: the app's store id, bundle id, Firebase project, Supabase ref and rating storefronts
the app's own funnel, engagement and health event names
the path to the app's event taxonomy file, for the drift guard
the app's project names and refs in the click paths

verify: `node scripts/monitoring/pulse.js --json --no-write` exits 0 with NO credentials configured, and every source reports status "unavailable" with a reason naming its variable. Zero false zeros is the whole point.
`git check-ignore -v .env.monitoring.local` matches an ignore rule, and monitoring/ is excluded from the build archive.
The suite passes, including the mutation checks: break the three-state guard in render.js and a named test must die.
With one credential set, that source reports real numbers while the others still say unavailable.
`/pulse` in Claude Code gathers crashes through the Firebase MCP server and narrates the snapshot.
